evidence_summary: The Tortoise Table lists Malva spp. as Safe to Feed, but the Korean retail name 아욱 is not accepted here as proof that a purchased product is Malva spp.
resolution: Keep blocked until Korean retail/botanical identity mapping is verified. If a specimen is confirmed as Malva spp., the general tortoise safety evidence can then be applied without converting it to Mediterranean Testudo direct evidence.

evidence_summary: Mint cannot safely receive one genus-wide verdict: garden mint/spearmint/apple mint are listed Safe to Feed, while peppermint and pennyroyal are Do not Feed.
resolution: Keep the generic Mentha spp. master blocked. Future safe assessments require species-level records such as Mentha spicata or Mentha suaveolens; peppermint and pennyroyal must remain separate negative taxa.

evidence_summary: No sufficiently specific tortoise-feeding evidence has been ingested for Korean minari/Oenanthe javanica. Similar English common names such as dropwort can refer to different genera and must not be substituted.
resolution: Keep unassessed until exact-taxon feeding or toxicology evidence suitable for tortoise applicability is verified.
